name: Skewbald
label: Dischord
lede: Minor Threat lost its guitarist to college, so Ian MacKaye and Jeff Nelson wrote songs in the Dischord House basement with two friends, recorded them once, and never played a show. The tape got traded for ten years, sometimes as lost Minor Threat.

eras.title: Minor Threat, minus a guitarist
eras.text: In fall 1981 D.C.'s biggest band stopped because guitarist Lyle Preslar went to college. Singer Ian MacKaye and drummer Jeff Nelson kept playing, down in the Dischord House basement, under a name they couldn't agree on.

years.cap: Minor Threat at the Wilson Center, Washington, April 1981: Lyle Preslar, Brian Baker and Ian MacKaye, with Jeff Nelson behind the kit
years.h: [[Lyle Preslar|c1b9b78e-691f-424d-8ce1-53c87c24d299]] goes to Northwestern, and [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] goes quiet
years.p: The breakup is a college schedule, not a fight. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]] don't want to stop playing, so they don't.

years.h: A basement, a borrowed guitarist and a bassist who'd never played bass
years.p: MacKaye sings and Nelson drums. [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] of the [[Untouchables|16d88df0-a2a9-4b3b-87ff-84e90e312d40]] plays guitar, and [[John Falls|44fd383a-ff3f-4028-8cc9-b01b71f5b2dc]], who'd played guitar briefly in [[Youth Brigade|7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c]], takes the bass.

years.h: MacKaye finds the name in a dictionary, Nelson picks the grocery store
years.p: MacKaye likes skewbald, an old word for a piebald horse. Nelson wants Grand Union, after a nearby supermarket. Dischord's band history gives the score: "Ian came across the word 'skewbald' in a dictionary and thought it was a better band name, but Jeff stuck by Grand Union."
years.xp: Wikipedia says the pair "were unable to favor either title, and the disagreement was never settled." Dischord's fix was to keep both, which is why the record is listed as Skewbald/Grand Union.

yt: Complete Inner Ear session, Nov 1981, with Rozzlyn Rangers
years.p: Dischord figures the only audience may have been Eric and Toni of Red C, at a practice. What survives is the November 1981 session, all of it.

eras.title: Minor Threat comes back
eras.text: Falls left, the band shrank to a trio, and then Minor Threat's return ended it.

years.h: Falls goes, and MacKaye moves from mic to bass
years.p: After the Inner Ear session John Falls leaves. MacKaye takes over bass, and he, Nelson and Janney practice as a trio for a short while.

years.h: Minor Threat reform in April, and Skewbald stops cold
years.p: Janney goes on to [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]] and later [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]].

eras.title: Not a Minor Threat bootleg
eras.text: For a decade the Inner Ear tape moved hand to hand on dubbed cassettes, sometimes labeled as Minor Threat. Dischord put it out as its 50th release, and the catalog number does the explaining.

yt: Side One (Sorry / Change for the Same)
years.h: Ten years on, the basement tape becomes Dischord No. 50
years.p: Three untitled songs, recorded by [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] at Inner Ear in November 1981, come out as a one-sided clear 7-inch. Two of them are joined into one track, so the EP is called 2 Songs.
years.xp:
Wikipedia puts side one at 2:54 and side two at 1:13, 4:07 in all. The titles are unofficial: Sorry / Change for the Same on one side, You're Not Fooling Me on the other.

The same session produced [[Rozzlyn Rangers|941e77e7-46b5-41e6-8260-79f0717bfc33]], the Dischord House theme song. Dischord says the tape was sometimes mistaken for unreleased [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]].

years.h: 2 Songs gets a CD in October 1997
years.p: Wikipedia dates the CD reissue to October 1997. Side two, You're Not Fooling Me, is the part to play.

years.h: The band that never played a show lands on a box set
years.p: Skewbald's Sorry / Change for the Same medley is on 20 Years of Dischord, the label's 3-CD anniversary set.
